newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Buddhists make do with tape from busy Tung.
newsitem.headline: HK's Buddhists make do with tape from busy Tung.

text.p: Buddhists awaiting a few words from Hong Kong's new leader had to settle for a taped message after a hectic schedule forced Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa to cut short a visit.

Tung, stretched by the demands of his first day in office on Tuesday after Hong Kong reverted to Chinese rule, spent only 90 seconds at a traditional Buddhist ceremony, the South China Morning Post said on Wednesday.
The 30,000 people who came for a blessing saw Tung make a few ceremonial gestures and leave behind a tape thanking the territory's 800,000 Buddhists for their support.
"It would have been nicer if he could have stayed longer or delivered his speech in person," one worshipper said.
Despite his absence, Tung was blessed by 250 senior monks in a 45-minute ceremony.
Britain handed back Hong Kong to China at midnight on Monday and Tung became the territory's first chief executive, replacing outgoing colonial governor Chris Patten.
